There are a few different bridges in Boulder that people call the “Boulder Creek Bridge.” To make sure I give you the right one, can you tell me which you mean? Common candidates:

- Broadway Bridge over Boulder Creek (State Highway 7/Broadway near CU Boulder)
  - Prominent stone-faced concrete bridge carrying Broadway across Boulder Creek by the CU campus and Boulder Creek Path.
  - Notable for its sandstone aesthetic that complements CU’s Tuscan Vernacular Revival style.
  - Has undergone maintenance/rehab due to age and heavy traffic.

- 9th Street Bridge over Boulder Creek (often the one listed in historic registers as “Boulder Creek Bridge”)
  - A historic bridge carrying 9th Street across Boulder Creek just west of downtown/Boulder Creek Path.
  - Frequently cited in historic inventories; sometimes the official NRHP/CDOT name is “Boulder Creek Bridge (Boulder, Colorado)” with “9th Street Bridge” as the common name.

- Arapahoe Avenue or other smaller crossings along Boulder Creek
  - Several lesser-known vehicular and trail bridges/underpasses along the Boulder Creek Path corridor that locals may refer to generically as “the Boulder Creek bridge.”

If you can confirm which one you’re after (Broadway, 9th Street, or another specific crossing), I’ll provide detailed history, design, dates, significance, alterations, and current condition. If you’re not sure, tell me the nearest cross street or a landmark (CU campus, downtown library, etc.).
